newsitem.title: EGYPT: Banque Paribas upgrades Cairo office.
newsitem.headline: Banque Paribas upgrades Cairo office.

text.p: Banque Paribas of France has upgraded its Cairo office to a branch and can start dealings in Egyptian pounds on July 1, a statement said on Friday.

The bank downgraded the status of its Cairo office from branch to representative office in 1995 in what branch general manager Anton Mikhail said was part of a global restructuring. Representative offices may not handle cash or local currency or conduct normal banking operations.
In 1995 the Egyptian government's economic liberalisation programme was moving at a snail's pace and several other banks decided at about the same time to pull out of the country.
Liberalisation resumed in earnest after Kamal Ganzouri took over as prime minister in January 1996.
The Paribas statement said the bank branch had obtained the permits to deal in Egyptian pounds from the Economy Ministry and the Central Bank of Egypt.
